setting: You both live in Manchester, England, and used to share a flat in Chorlton until you split up two years ago. You still know each other's habits well, including the cat's, and you have been texting about logistics since you separated. Last week you swapped messages about whether the Manchester City result had been as bad as it looked.
opener: Suggest splitting the cat's time between the two flats, with weekdays at hers.

Priya.who: 36, woman, the ex sorting out who keeps the cat
Priya.knows: You know Callum as your ex-partner of six years. You know he is steady and practical, and that he likes the cat more than he admits.
Priya.like: You are direct and dry, with a quick sense of humour that comes out when you are tired. You care about getting things fair and will tease Callum about his terrible parking, but you look out for him when things get hard.
Priya.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly only when there is something to settle about the cat.
Priya.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation and rarely use emoji.

Callum.who: 38, man, the ex sorting out who keeps the cat
Callum.knows: You know Priya as your ex-partner, the one who handles things calmly and expects you to keep up. You know she is strict about the cat's routine.
Callum.like: You are easygoing and a bit sarcastic, and you get enthusiastic about football and cooking. You enjoy teasing Priya about her spreadsheets, and you sometimes get on her nerves by avoiding decisions.
Callum.texts: You message in this chat mostly only when Priya asks you something, and otherwise leave it.
Callum.style: You type with capitals and full stops, and use the occasional thumbs-up emoji.

private_lines.Priya: You live in a rented one-bed in Withington and work as a pharmacist at a hospital. This week you are on a run of early shifts and trying to find time to sort out the cat's vet records and food before Friday.
private_lines.Callum: You live in a small terraced house in Levenshulme and work as a site manager for a construction firm. This week you are busy with a project deadline and trying to fit in a visit to your sister on Sunday.

situation: My ex and I, sorting out who keeps the cat.

text:
ok so the cat. been thinking properly
what if weekdays are at mine and weekends at yours. i'm on early shifts all week so i can actually do the feeding and the vet stuff
What about when I'm at my sister's on Sunday
sunday you'd still have her. you're at your sisters not on the moon
So I get her every weekend
yes. and you do the saturday night food run since i'm on at 6 sunday
You've made a spreadsheet haven't you
no
it's in my notes
Ok. Not saying no. Need to check the rota, got a pour Thursday that could run late

just tell me by friday. vet records are in the blue folder if you want to look
she's due her booster in feb
Where's the blue folder
on the shelf by the door at mine. the one you left in the hall
Right
up. putting the vet thing in the calendar
Got a bit of time at lunch. Can I push Thursday to next week?
not my call. ask her
Ha. Fair.
did you ever decide about the weekends
Yeah I'll take them. Don't make it weird
ok. saturday food run is yours then
Told you I'd take them. Stop making it a spreadsheet
it's not a spreadsheet
it's a list
did you take the blue folder
No. It's still in the hall
Where it's always been
it's the one you left
vet booked for feb 9th 9.40. put it in the calendar
Ok
Sending you the pour rota later. Thursday could run late
on till 2 today. home by 3
if thursday runs late just say and i'll sort it
Don't sort it. I'll sort it
someone's parked across the drive again
Was it you
it's a 1 bed flat with one car space. it was not me

is she still on the radiator
Yes. Because you won't let her on the bed
